svg.title: Key Manager architecture
svg.desc: Block diagram of key_manager. The CPU u_cpu (picorv32_wrapper) holds the PicoRV32 RV32EMC core, and the ROM and SRAM interfaces u_rom_if (parity) and u_sram_if (scrambling and parity), which connect to the 16 KiB ROM and 32 KiB SRAM hard macros outside the block. The CPU AXI4-Lite master drives the crossbar u_xbar. The crossbar serves four internal subordinates, u_kmcsr, u_kpv, u_mailbox and u_drbg_sampler, and six external ports: the key CSRs of Adams Bridge, OTBN, AES, KMAC and HMAC, and the SEP eFuse controller. u_otp_demux decodes the eFuse port by register map: offsets in the MAP, CTRL and MMR register maps have address bits 31 to 12 replaced by OTP_EFUSE_REMAP_BASE and leave on efuse_req_o, and every other offset is answered with SLVERR by u_otp_err_slv. The CPU receives three interrupts: km_irq from u_kmcsr, the mailbox interrupt from u_mailbox and the Adams Bridge ML-KEM shared-key interrupt. u_kmcsr receives otp_data_i and drives recoverable_err_o and the scrambler, SRAM lock and execute-mode controls of u_cpu, which returns its error events. The CPU trap drives unrecoverable_err_o and is ORed with wipe_state_i; the rising edge of the result is a single-cycle wipe pulse that drives both u_kpv and u_kmcsr. The SEP host reaches u_mailbox, whose two FIFOs are MAILBOX_DEPTH words deep, through mbox_sep_req_i and receives mbox_irq_to_sep_o. u_drbg_sampler receives the DRBG AXI-Stream. u_reset_conditioner turns cold_rst_ni, warm_rst_ni, test_en_i, scan_rst_ni and the soft_rst_n output of u_kmcsr into the cold and warm resets of every instance; the warm reset is held for MIN_RESET_CYCLES cycles.
